verdict.rationale: Raygun documents its own source map decoding, which turns minified JavaScript errors into readable traces with source snippets. Maps are fetched automatically when public, or can be uploaded manually through the JS source map center or an API that uses an external access token, so CI uploads are possible by scripting the API. The story specifically asks for a CLI or bundler plugin, and neither appears in the evidence. Missing for 10: an official upload CLI, bundler plugins (webpack/Vite/etc.), documented CI workflow examples, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can upload JavaScript source maps from CI — via CLI or bundler plugin — so production stack traces show my original source, not minified frames

citations.quote: Raygun uses them to take un-readable errors generated from minified JavaScript and translate them to be readable and to include code snippets from your source.
you can also manually upload source maps either through our website using the `JS source map center` or via our API
